newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-SARFU CALLS UPON TSHWETE FOR SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SARFU CALLS UPON TSHWETE FOR SUPPORT.

text.p: The South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU) on Thursday called upon Minister of Sport Steve Tshwete to issue "a statement of approval and support for SARFU and their management of South African rugby".

SARFU's executive committee asked the minister in a press statement to acknowledge that his ministry had no proof of the mismanagement in South African rugby which has been alleged by former Transvaal Rugby Union vice-president Brian van Rooyen.
"This matter is whipping up emotions without good reason and is detrimental to the good of the game," SARFU senior vice-president Mluleki George said.
SARFU's chief executive officer Riaan Oberholzer said that the van Rooyen dossier had been discredited by both SARFU and by the Department of Sport's Mthobi Tyamzashe.

"They have not produced any proof of any kind of impropriety in South African rugby. We are willing to meet with a team from the ministry to discuss the allegations as we agreed at our meeting with the minister, if he feels it is necessary," Oberholzer said.

"Since all the allegations arising from the dossier have been shown to be unfounded, the executive committee believes such a meeting may be unnecessary. This whole affair is costing time and, more importantly, money that could be spent on rugby development."
SARFU president Louis Luyt said: "We are hoping that the ministry will accept there is no need to pursue this matter."
Oberholzer added that SARFU was always working on improving the perception of South African rugby "in the interest of our country".
"We welcome the ministry's valuable assistance in this goal but perhaps our energies could be better spent promoting rugby together."
